title: Run takeover
summary: Registered deployment-runs get reads expose read-only supersedes_run_id and superseded_by_run_id in default, selected-field and full reads, outside portable snapshots; human summaries name set links as supersedes and superseded by. Cut the superseding release while member QA runs; the takeover moves each live execution with its leases and host turns, and owners continue the same execution ID. Inherit cases in a moved chained plan run find their predecessor on the successor run once takeover lineage proves the move, though the frozen roster keeps the admitting run; a predecessor still not found blocks naming the unlinked run or the missing requirement. Successor creation skips cancelled and superseded runs on its project and target whose flow is its own or a retired flow whose active successor it runs on; an active predecessor flow is not followed, and carried QA keeps counting as inherited across that flow change. An executing predecessor waiting on QA with open QA, never while settling, is superseded first because it occupies the target, and every never-started run created after it is absorbed: members and QA move and the run is cancelled. Otherwise only the newest earlier run is considered: created (prepared or not) and failed predecessors qualify without open QA, without reaching past an ineligible candidate. It evaluates that candidate through complete frozen QA selections. An incomplete historical selection refuses with reviewed operator repair recovery before resumption. Original source and target identities remain authoritative. A containing successor on the same flow, or the active successor of the retired flow, and target takes over waiting members under existing QA and approval rules. The takeover settles the old run in the same transaction, moving its members through one batched removal and one batched admission so its cost does not grow with the member count. Without shared QA or approval, a member stays in the old run only when the old run already closed it; every unclosed member, including a passed-but-open, refused or non-final one, moves, except one whose hard-block blocker neither moves, enrolls in the successor as carried work, nor has shipped: it is set aside on the old run with its QA, the successor's notice names it as left on the run it took over with its blocker, and the first release after the blocker ships enrolls it, so the dependent never refuses the whole creation. The old run then reads succeeded when it delivered at least one member and cancelled when none stayed, so it never sits executing without a driver. A settled run's still-live driver has status and stage changes refused with deployment_run_superseded, naming the successor to watch instead of a re-drive. At a failed stage, that refusal exits successfully without changing the settled status or stage, emitting failure events or running a failure trace; a refused succeeded gate refuses the takeover with takeover_settlement_refused. With shared QA or approval every unclosed member that is not set aside that way moves and the old run is cancelled, so no approval is skipped. While a live steering seat covers the project only the seat holder or the older run's creating session may take it over, live driver or not; other sessions are refused with takeover_reserved_for_steering and report the landing to steering. start-for-item creates, takes over, enrolls and validates in one transaction, so any refusal writes nothing and an item the takeover moved is enrolled once. The successor is not a retry: moved members keep their QA identities and executions, while their selections, snapshots and plan pins re-derive from live obligations and attachments as a fresh run's do; only a plan whose moved rows already ran keeps its ownership and pinned cases. A requirement waived since is skipped like a retracted one. Takeover enrollment honors pre-start operator parks on the superseded run, any absorbed never-started runs and their predecessors until the item lands again or add-item makes it the successor's member; add-item clears only the target run's own entry, so predecessor entries stay as audit records. Creation names each inherited exclusion with its source run, reason, removal time and expiry. Takeover entries recorded before transferred_to_run_id existed were backfilled by migration 0116, so they read as transfers, never parks. A successor whose pin carries an item removed at item QA can enroll it again. Automatic releases awaiting a later release, a set-aside or a member whose candidate is outside the frozen lineage, are not inherited, so a successor whose pin contains the candidate enrolls it. Ordinary creation still enrolls the delivery-ready work the newer candidate carries before dependency validation, so a merged blocker those members need is co-enrolled; an inadmissible new member refuses the whole creation and takeover. Only a recorded retry_of keeps a frozen roster unwidened. Unlocked creation prepares carried-work facts against the waiting run when takeover would settle it succeeded, projecting unclosed member movement in a transaction that rolls back without removal audits, notices or settlement; cancelled takeovers retain the preceding succeeded release as their base. Locked validation rechecks settlement against current state. Exhausted creation preparation names the original create or start-for-item command and idempotency key as recovery. The successor's carried work compares from the run it settled, each repository comparison counted on its own; a comparison the repository cannot answer records carried work as unknown with its named reason and recovery rather than failing creation, and the settled run's own carried work is recorded after creation commits. Creation refuses up front when the caller's machine could not drive a self-deploy run. Takeover preserves running QA execution state, custody, heartbeat authority, host turns and leases; owners continue the same execution ID. Open walks carry intact to the successor; never hold a release for an open walk. The creation receipt lists each carried open execution in carried_execution_ids and the stderr takeover note names them, and an owner mid-walk gets no takeover notice. A set-aside member's unfinished QA also survives its former run ending and does not hold that run's completion gates. Owner notices explicitly name that preservation and the later enrollment. Creation records the successor's bound source commits before admitting transferred members; a bound project member can transfer, while a project the flow carries no source for still refuses. Creation preserves admission for exactly the transferred members, identified by transferred_to_run_id on predecessor removal records, including members in implementing or reviewing-implementation; only newly enrolled members must be delivery-ready. Their QA rows and in-progress executions retain identity across executing and failed predecessors. At execution context and resume, a member with any open landing attempt or in implementing or reviewing-implementation is set aside without retracting unsettled QA or stopping executions, and the members depending on it through hard-block edges, transitively, are set aside with it. A later enrolling run on the same flow and target adopts those identities. Frozen containment remains authoritative for remaining members. Generic multi-flow create resolves one source commit, creates flows in order with KEY:FLOW keys and their own environments, and cancels runs made in that call when a later create refuses. A still-deploying predecessor is named in the creation receipt and retains target occupancy. A superseded driver exits successfully naming its successor. A run binding another project's source, when created or started, also supersedes each bound project's never-started run on a same-named environment whose pin its bound commit for that project contains: members and QA move, the stale run is cancelled, and removals and cancellation name the superseding run and bound commit. A stale run with a live driver, or whose pin the carrier does not contain, keeps its custody and the carrier's custody names it as holder.
